text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Budget cuts are necessary to stop state running deficit; despite strong economic growth state debt has increased and is intolerable, Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto says.
- Direct elections make presidential campaigns more populist and president's leading position in foreign policy is not suited to this, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen says.
- Over half Conservative party MPs support idea of limiting presidential powers in foreign policy issues, a study shows. @
- Farm investments have increased and already thousands of Finnish farmers now make a million or more markka in turnover, study by Statictics Finland shows.
- Almost-forgotten tradition of cattle-calling was revived in Finnish championships at the weekend in middle Finland.
- Construction sector may, in regions, be near overheating and scarcity of skilled workers is becoming a problem, sector representatives say. @

- Moscow and Russian markets open new opportunities for Finnish economic life -- Finns should invest more in lobbying in Moscow, says Kari Jalas, new managing director at Central Chamber of Commerce of Finland.
- Finnish ministers own only very limited amount of stocks, a financial study shows. After September, also high government officials are obliged to report their financial commitments.
- Farm production prices have fallen most compared to other European Union countries. @
- Markets in Far East have growing importance for Finnish metal industry, says Timo Airaksinen, director of industry and business relations at the Metal industry's central union.

- Current powers of president do not fit democracy; if plan to shrink president's foreign policy powers is not approved, authority in domestic issues should be limited, says Ville Itala, chairman of the Parliament's constitutional committee. -- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
